_comment: This repo's own CLAUDE.md sections (outside the shared:rules block), each rule classified for the shared checks' rules-gated (tools/checks: its gates.json holds the vocabulary and the shared block's rows). Paths are from the workspace top. A `gate` row's test is run by ./dev.sh check (the suite), which is why the dev.sh rows name it; a hook row's test is run by check-hooks.sh and test/hooks.test.js. Held by test/gates-json.test.js (parses, one unedited block, and `checks one rules-gated` is ok here), which ./dev.sh check runs. A prose row whose probe is not built is listed in TODO.md.

rules.rule: This engine is the primary way to read a web page here, not a fallback.
rules.note: a WebFetch or browser navigation to a host with a working recipe is refused; check-hooks.sh also RUNS every copy on a covered host and requires a block

rules.rule: Building a SECOND recipe on a known host? Read the page first.
rules.why: a habit before building: nothing marks the moment a second recipe is started, so nothing can ask whether `dev.sh page` was read first

rules.rule: Observations are earned
rules.note: recordObservation is a guarded write; the trial runner is its only sanctioned caller

rules.rule: Writes are BLOCKED outside a sanctioned path.
rules.note: lib/writeGuard.js refuses an unauthorized write; guard.test.js holds that every definition-mutating db.js export is guarded

rules.rule: Never use raw SQL or inline node -e to change data.
rules.note: store-guard refuses a raw sqlite3 or shell write to a store cli.json names; the inline half is no-inline-blobs-here

rules.rule: status is earned, never asserted.
rules.why: no check can tell an earned status from an asserted one: the write guard (test/guard.test.js) holds who may write a status, not that a run chose the value

rules.rule: Do NOT retry, that already failed
rules.note: the hook blocks an unattended re-run; the CLI refuses it again (lib/blockedGuard.js, test/blocked-guard.test.js)

rules.rule: Never write an inline script blob. This one is ENFORCED, not advised.
Prove a parameter does something.
rules.why: the proof is a LIVE run (audit.js params: a browser, minutes per site), which ./dev.sh check does not run; the offline half (param_probe_values declared) is not a gate either. TODO.md holds wiring it

rules.rule: The recipe is the unique document; the actions it performs are not.
rules.why: what is site-specific is a judgement; audit.js inline and repeats report candidates as warnings, never errors

rules.rule: Never run two live audits or sweeps at once
rules.why: contention is between processes and sessions; nothing inside one run can see another

rules.rule: Confirm before storing an action.
rules.why: the answer is Jacob's, given in conversation

rules.rule: Before committing: ./dev.sh check
rules.note: check-json.test.js holds the check's gates and its red/green verdict; the commit itself is held by the githooks setup installs

rules.rule: dev.sh is the human-readable layer over those CLIs
rules.note: dev.sh documents every subcommand it implements and implements every one it documents; the CLIs' own lists are not compared with this section (TODO.md)

rules.rule: A warning you have checked gets waived, not re-derived.
rules.note: a waiver needs a date and a reason, silences only its rule, and never an error

rules.section: How the shared rules apply here
rules.rule: query.js efficiency tracks output_chars

rules.section: How the shared rules apply here
rules.rule: Write it at the moment you notice it.
rules.why: the moment something is noticed is in a session's head; no check sees it

rules.section: How the shared rules apply here
rules.rule: Consumers see what audits cannot.
rules.why: a reason to read and relay consumer reports, not a behaviour a check can hold

rules.section: How the shared rules apply here
rules.rule: Commit and push to origin master right away
rules.why: when to commit is a habit; push-gate (tools/hooks) holds what may be pushed, not that it was

rules.rule: Job applications are prepare-then-confirm, one yes per batch
rules.note: the engine refuses a submit without its approval input (zero submit attempts at the fixture); that the yes covered exactly the presented batch is Jacob's, in conversation

rules.rule: Never create an account, or do anything else public or irreversible
rules.why: an account form is an ordinary form until a person reads it; the submit half is applications-confirm

rules.rule: Never enter real credentials without Jacob.
rules.why: a real credential and a fixture one are the same shape to code

rules.rule: Credential-shaped values are caller-supplied params at run time, never written into a stored recipe.
rules.note: a literal credential in a recipe is refused at EXPORT, not at register (TODO.md); run telemetry is redacted in db.js logRun (test/run-redaction.test.js)

rules.rule: Never attempt to bypass bot detection.
rules.why: a bypass is an intent, not a shape; a detected wall is marked blocked-attn, which the blocked-attn gate then holds

rules.rule: Captured handoff values go to gitignored mode-600 files.
rules.note: the gitignore half only: that every captured-value file is written mode 600 is not asserted by one test (TODO.md)

rules.rule: test/rules-sync.test.js checks this list
Every section outside the markers has a row in gates.json
